To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Facebook management behaviors are not common but are related to the size and political homogeneity of one's social network.
Facebook users engage in self-presentation strategies related to political views, but only to a limited extent.

(1) Facebook users are not actively managing political disclosures and content exposure on Facebook, but as network sizes increase users engage in more disclosure and management behaviors; and (2) individuals with stronger political beliefs engage in greater management behaviors, possibly in an effort to reduce cognitive dissonance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the self presentation of political views on social media.
the ways in which individuals utilize Facebook as a platform for self presentation.
how individuals manage their political communication via Facebook and the factors that influence these management behaviors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Facebook management behaviors are not a common or widespread occurrence.
Facebook management is a complex process, and that it varies by the user's political views and network size.
the majority of Facebook users do not manage their political disclosures or exposure, but those who do are more politically engaged and have larger social networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of Facebook users do not engage in strategic management of their own political disclosures and content exposure.
Facebook users are not actively managing the content they are consuming or disclosing, but they do make an effort to do so when their networks are large and when their political views are strong.
Facebook users are not actively engaging in the strategic self management of their political disclosures or the content to which they expose themselves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Facebook management behaviors are related to both social network and political factors.
the management of political communication on social media is a complex process that is influenced by both individual characteristics and network characteristics.
the management of political content on social media is a relatively new phenomenon and one that has yet to be widely adopted by users.
